title: Consumption Chooser Playbook — Hosted, Dedicated, Private
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook helps product, solutions, and engineering teams recommend an optimal Redwood consumption mode (Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private) for a customer workload. It combines a decision matrix, SLO/latency and cost heuristics, migration steps, pricing impact guidance, and a short checklist for technical validation. Use this when engaging customers during discovery, scoping, pricing conversations, and migration planning.

Audience
--------
- Solutions Engineers and Sales Engineers
- Customer Success and Onboarding
- Product and GTM leads sizing consumption and SLAs
- Platform/Infra leads for deployment gating

High-level guidance
-------------------
- Start with Hosted for developer proof-of-concepts and light production workloads (non-SLA critical).
- Recommend Dedicated when predictable throughput and single-tenant GPU pools are required (SLO-backed, high QPS / heavy KV cache needs).
- Recommend Private for regulated workloads requiring VPC/on-prem, strict data residency, or on-prem integration.

Decision matrix (quick view)
---------------------------
Provide this table to stakeholders to align on selection. Scores are normalized heuristic indicators (1 = low relevance, 5 = high relevance).

| Decision factor                      | Hosted API | Dedicated | Private |
|-------------------------------------|:----------:|:--------:|:-------:|
| Regulatory / data residency need     |     1      |    2     |    5    |
| Required SLA (availability/latency) |     2      |    5     |    5    |
| Predictable throughput (QPS)        |     2      |    5     |    4    |
| Cost sensitivity (per-token)        |     3      |    4     |    2    |
| Need for custom infra/networking    |     1      |    3     |    5    |
| Model customization & private model |     2      |    4     |    5    |
| KV cache locality / session affinity|     2      |    5     |    4    |

Interpreting the matrix
-----------------------
- Hosted: best for rapid iteration and unpredictable, low-to-medium sustained traffic. Lower setup friction, pay-as-you-go pricing, built-in fallbacks.
- Dedicated: best when you need SLA-backed uptime and consistent latency under load (reserved GPU pools, capacity commits).
- Private: best for compliance or deep network integrations — higher setup and ops overhead with contractual licensing.

SLO and performance heuristics
-----------------------------
Map application-level expectations to Redwood SLO recommendations:

- Latency-sensitive interactive apps (chat, autocomplete): target p50 < 50ms token generation, p95 < 300ms for common prompts. Recommend Dedicated with real-time priority routing or Hosted with upgraded SLA and priority lanes for small tenants.
- Batch/analytics workloads (embeddings, reranking): throughput-first; acceptable p95 can be multi-second. Hosted often sufficient; Dedicated or Private for very large batch windows.
- Hard-regulated low-latency: Private or Dedicated with colocated VPC connectivity and dedicated kernel/quantization profiles.

Cost/packaging impact (high level)
----------------------------------
- Hosted: per-token pricing and embedding unit bills. Fastest time-to-value; cost scales with traffic.
- Dedicated: committed monthly/annual capacity with overage pricing. Predictable unit economics; recommended for consistent > X tokens/month (see heuristics below).
- Private: platform licensing + support; host bears infra cost. Best for customers who must own infra or pass strict procurement controls.

Heuristic thresholds to discuss with customers (examples to quantify sizing)
- If sustained 24h average QPS > 200 and predictable workload: consider Dedicated.
- If monthly token usage > 1 billion with predictable pattern: Dedicated likely more economical.
- If customer requires 3rd-party model binaries and HSM integration: Private.

Sample cost sensitivity table (illustrative)
| Scenario                            | Likely pick |
|------------------------------------|-------------|
| Prototype, < 250k tokens/month     | Hosted      |
| Production SaaS, steady 500k/day   | Dedicated   |
| Regulated data, audit + on-prem    | Private     |

Migration playbook (Hosted -> Dedicated/Private)
------------------------------------------------
1) Discovery and constraints (owner: Solutions Eng)
   - Collect SLO targets, peak QPS, token distribution (prompt/response lengths), embedding throughput, security/regulatory needs.
   - Required network topology: VPC peering, private link, or on-prem connectors.
2) Capacity and model compatibility (owner: Eng-Platform + Serving Runtime)
   - Run profiling using the customer prompt sets. Capture p50/p95 latencies, KV hit rates, and token distribution.
   - Select model variants and quantization profile that meet quality targets.
3) Pricing & contractual alignment (owner: Sales/Finance)
   - Propose committed capacity tiers, burst allowances, and SLA terms (RTO/RPO, latency SLAs).
   - Define migration credits/intro discounts if moving from Hosted.
4) Integration and security validation (owner: Eng-Private-Deployments or Infra)
   - Validate network setup (VPN, peering), KMS/HSM integration tests, and audit log forwarding.
5) Canary migration (owner: Customer Success + Platform)
   - Route 5–10% of production traffic to Dedicated/Private variant with canary rollback plan. Monitor telemetry for 72h.
6) Full cutover and post-cutover audit
   - Complete cutover during planned low-traffic window. Run the post-cutover checklist (observability sanity, billing reconciliation, SLO ramp).

Technical validation checklist (short)
- Model parity: run 1000 sample prompts comparing outputs for statistical drift (per-prompt token diff and embedding cosine similarity thresholds).
- Latency profile: verify p50/p95/p99 against agreed SLOs using synthetic and replayer traffic.
- KV cache effectiveness: measure steady-state KV hit rate; ensure session affinity config is applied.
- Failure modes: simulate node failure and verify fallback to variant models/regions.

Configuration reference snippets
-------------------------------
Example routing policy snippet (YAML) to prefer Dedicated for SLA-tagged routes:

routing_policy:
  - name: sla_priority
    match:
      route_labels:
        - "payment-processing"
    prefer:
      - pool: dedicated-us-west
        min_capacity: 0.8
      - pool: hosted-fallback
        max_latency_ms: 500

Example autoscale policy for Dedicated pool:
{
  "pool": "dedicated-us-west",
  "min_replicas": "4",
  "max_replicas": "32",
  "scale_metric": "request_tokens_per_second",
  "target_value": "2000"
}

Rollout and rollback guardrails
-------------------------------
- Canary windows: minimum 72 hours with detailed telemetry (latency, error rate, token mismatch metric).
- Automatic rollback triggers: +20% p95 latency increase, error-rate delta > 0.5% absolute, embedding drift > 0.08 median cosine drop.
- Manual rollback checklist: pause new deployments, shift traffic to previous route, open incident ticket with SRE and Product.

Roadmap & product asks (what product should improve to reduce friction)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
- Short-term (0–3 months): Add a migration credits config page in Console; provide preflight workload profiler available to Solutions Engs.
- Mid-term (3–9 months): One-click Dedicated trial with auto-sizing recommendation and cost estimate; improved telemetry diff UI for model parity checks.
- Long-term (9–18 months): Automated fidelity negotiation engine to dynamically shift requests between pools based on cost and SLOs.

Customer-facing talking points (concise)
--------------------------------------
- "Start on Hosted to move fast; we’ll profile your workload and recommend whether Dedicated saves cost and improves reliability."
- "Dedicated gives predictable latency and an SLA backed by reserved GPUs—good when your product depends on consistent realtime response."
- "Private deployment is for regulated or air-gapped environments where network and audit controls are mandatory."

---------------------

Feedback and iteration
----------------------
